requirements.title: Push option validation
requirements.rationale: An agent that mistypes an option must learn it before anything is written, from one line that names the option and the reason.

criteria.condition: a push arrives with at most 16 push options, each at most 1,024 bytes long and each either without the `parley.` prefix or a well-formed one of `parley.change`, `parley.target=<branch>`, `parley.title=<text>`, `parley.intent=<text>`, `parley.draft` and `parley.session=<id>`, including a push with no options
criteria.action: accept the options, ignore every option whose name does not begin with `parley.`, and split each `parley.` option at its first `=` into a name and a value
criteria.contract: the validated option set: change requested (true when `parley.change` or `parley.target` is present), target, title, intent, draft, session id; no refusal

setup: a session linker stub that accepts every reference
check.pseudocode: in internal/gitserver/pushoptions_test.go, a table over option lists that must all be accepted, asserting the parsed result of each: {[] -> nothing set; ['parley.change'] -> change; ['parley.target=release'] -> target 'release' and change implied; ['parley.draft','parley.change'] -> draft and change; ['parley.title=a=b'] -> title 'a=b'; ['parley.title=' + 200 characters, 10 of them multi-byte] -> accepted; ['parley.intent=' + text making the whole option exactly 1024 bytes] -> accepted; ['ci.skip','other=1','parley.change'] -> change, the two others ignored; 16 options of which 10 have no `parley.` prefix -> accepted; ['parley.session=<id>'] with a session linker that accepts -> session id set}; assert no refusal in any case

criteria.condition: a push option is a `parley.` name that is not one of the six, or a `parley.` option given twice, or `parley.change` or `parley.draft` written with `=`, or `parley.target`, `parley.title`, `parley.intent` or `parley.session` without `=` or with an empty value, or a `parley.target` for which `refs/heads/<value>` is not a well-formed git ref name, or a `parley.title` longer than 200 characters
criteria.action: refuse the whole push with a message that names the first invalid option in the order sent and its reason
criteria.contract: a refusal with the message `invalid push option <name>: <reason>`, where `<reason>` is `unknown option`, `given more than once`, `takes no value`, `value required`, `not a valid branch name` or `longer than 200 characters`

setup: a session linker stub that accepts every reference
check.pseudocode: in internal/gitserver/pushoptions_test.go, a table over option lists and the expected message: {['parley.titel=x'] -> 'invalid push option parley.titel: unknown option'; ['parley.change','parley.change'] -> 'invalid push option parley.change: given more than once'; ['parley.title=a','parley.title=b'] -> '... parley.title: given more than once'; ['parley.change=1'] -> '... parley.change: takes no value'; ['parley.draft='] -> '... parley.draft: takes no value'; ['parley.target'] and ['parley.target='] -> '... parley.target: value required'; ['parley.title='], ['parley.intent'], ['parley.session='] -> '... value required'; ['parley.target=a..b'], ['parley.target=bad name'], ['parley.target=x.lock'] -> '... parley.target: not a valid branch name'; ['parley.title=' + 201 characters] -> '... parley.title: longer than 200 characters'; ['parley.draft=1','parley.bogus'] -> names parley.draft, the first one}; assert the result is a refusal and its message equals the expected text exactly

criteria.condition: a push carries more than 16 push options, or any push option longer than 1,024 bytes counting its name and value
criteria.action: refuse the whole push, whether or not the options at fault have the `parley.` prefix
criteria.contract: a refusal with the message `too many push options: at most 16 are accepted` for the count, checked first, and `invalid push option <name>: longer than 1024 bytes` for the length, where `<name>` is the text before the first `=`

check.pseudocode: in internal/gitserver/pushoptions_test.go, a table: {17 options 'x1'..'x17' -> 'too many push options: at most 16 are accepted'; 17 options of which the first is 'parley.bogus' -> the too-many message (the count is checked first); ['parley.intent=' + text making the option 1025 bytes] -> 'invalid push option parley.intent: longer than 1024 bytes'; ['note=' + 1021 bytes] (1026 bytes, no parley prefix) -> 'invalid push option note: longer than 1024 bytes'}; assert refusal and exact message

criteria.condition: the session linker (the interface SessionLinker of internal/gitserver, to which package 49 hands its session-linking check) does not accept the value of `parley.session`, or no session linker is registered (the session does not exist, was created by another user while the caller is not the admin token, or belongs to a workspace that is neither the pushed workspace, its parent nor one of its forks)
criteria.action: ask the session linker with the caller, the session id and the pushed workspace, and refuse the whole push
criteria.contract: a refusal with the message `invalid push option parley.session: unknown session`

check.pseudocode: in internal/gitserver/pushoptions_test.go, with a session linker stub scripted to refuse: validate ['parley.session=3f2c…'] for caller U and workspace 'demo'; assert the stub was called once with (U, that id, 'demo'); assert refusal with message 'invalid push option parley.session: unknown session'; a second case with the value 'not-a-uuid' and the stub refusing gives the same message; a third case with no session linker registered gives the same message

criteria.condition: the session linker fails with an internal error
criteria.action: refuse the whole push and never treat the session as accepted
criteria.contract: a refusal with the message `internal error; try again`

check.pseudocode: in internal/gitserver/pushoptions_test.go, with a session linker stub that returns an internal error: validate ['parley.session=<id>']; assert refusal with message 'internal error; try again'; assert the result carries no session id

criteria.condition: a git client pushes with push options that validation refuses with message M
criteria.action: answer the push without storing the pack, without evaluating the push rules, without moving a ref, without emitting an event and without touching a change, and report the refusal on the side band once and on every ref of the push
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with a receive-pack result holding `unpack ok`, then `ng <ref> M` for every ref of the push, and one side-band line `error: M`; the git client prints `remote: error: M` and `! [remote rejected] <ref> (M)` and exits non-zero; no object, ref, event or change is written; the request counts as `refused` in `parley_git_requests_total`

requirements.title: The session of a push
requirements.rationale: A consumer of the event stream follows what an agent does by its session, also for pushes that involve no change.

criteria.condition: an accepted push carries a valid `parley.session=<id>`
criteria.action: give the session id to every `parley.git.push` event of the push, whether or not a change is involved
criteria.contract: each `parley.git.push` event of the push has `session_id` equal to `<id>`

criteria.condition: an accepted push carries no `parley.session` option
criteria.action: emit the `parley.git.push` events of the push with a null session
criteria.contract: each `parley.git.push` event of the push has `session_id` null

criteria.condition: an accepted push records a version through the ref-updated stage of package 22, or its mapping opens a change
criteria.action: hand the session id of `parley.session` to the ref writer of package 18, which gives it to the stage, and pass it with every open request of the mapping; pass no session when the option is absent
criteria.contract: the version recorded for the push and the open requests carry the push's session id, or none; with none, the defaults of the change component apply

requirements.title: Mapping each pushed branch to a change
requirements.rationale: An agent's push should open a change or add a version without a second call, and a plain branch should stay a plain branch.

criteria.action: for any accepted push, consider only its created or updated `refs/heads/*` refs for change mapping, one at a time in command order, and skip tags, refs in other namespaces and deletes without a line and without change activity
criteria.contract: change activity and side-band lines exist only for created or updated branches, in command order; `parley.change` on a push of only tags or only branch deletes has no effect and is not an error

setup: a mapper built with a fake change service that records every call (find open change of a source, record version, open change) and returns scripted results, and a recorder for side-band lines
check.pseudocode: in internal/gitserver/changemap_test.go: run the mapper with `parley.change` over the accepted updates, in this order, [create refs/tags/v1, update refs/heads/b, delete refs/heads/gone, create refs/notes/x, create refs/heads/a]; assert the fake saw find-open-change calls for exactly 'b' then 'a', in that order; assert two lines were sent, the first for b; a second run with only [create refs/tags/v1, delete refs/heads/gone] and `parley.change` makes no call, sends no line and returns no error

criteria.condition: a created or updated branch of an accepted push is the source of a change in state `open` or `draft`
criteria.action: have the ref-updated stage that package 22 registers with the ref writer of package 18 record a new version of kind `push` for that change with the branch's new head, inside the commit step of the ref update, whatever options the push carries and without checking `changes:write`; the mapping takes the version the ref writer reports and records none itself
criteria.contract: one version of kind `push` is recorded on the existing change, in the store transaction of the ref update; the mapping makes no record-version call and no open call for the branch; no change is opened

requirements.title: What a push-opened change is
requirements.rationale: The push options describe the changes a push opens and nothing else; the change of a fork's branch belongs to the parent, where it will land.

criteria.condition: the mapping opens a change for a branch pushed to a repository workspace
criteria.action: open the change in the pushed workspace with the source `{pushed workspace slug, branch}`, the target branch given by `parley.target` or none when the option is absent, and the pushing credential's actor as author
criteria.contract: the change belongs to the pushed workspace; its source is the pushed branch; its target is the `parley.target` value, or the workspace's default branch when the option is absent; its author is the pushing credential's actor

requirements.title: What the git client sees
requirements.rationale: The agent reads the number of its change and the version of its push from the output of `git push`, with no further request.

criteria.condition: the ref writer reports a version recorded for a branch of the push, or the mapping records one on an existing change after a lost race
criteria.action: send the side-band line `change <workspace>#<number> version <n>` for that branch, where `<workspace>` is the slug of the workspace the change belongs to
criteria.contract: one side-band line `change <workspace>#<number> version <n>`, shown by git as `remote: change <workspace>#<number> version <n>`; the line carries no URL

requirements.title: Failures never fail the push
requirements.rationale: The commits are the agent's work; a change that cannot be opened is a message to act on, not a reason to throw the push away.

criteria.condition: the change component refuses to open a change for a branch because the target branch does not exist (including a `parley.target` that names no branch), the branch has no commits ahead of the target, a merge commit is among the commits ahead of the target, the intent is empty while `changes.require_intent` is true and `parley.draft` was not given, or for another reason that carries an `error_type`
criteria.action: keep the push accepted and send `warning: no change for <branch>: <reason>` for that branch, with the reason of the refusal
criteria.contract: the line `warning: no change for <branch>: <reason>` with `<reason>` equal to `target branch <target> does not exist (target_not_found)`, `no commits ahead of <target> (nothing_to_land)`, `merge commits are not supported (merge_commits_unsupported)`, `intent is required; push with -o parley.intent=<text> or -o parley.draft (intent_required)`, or for any other refusal its message followed by its `error_type` in parentheses; no change is created

execution_paths.title: An agent opens a change by pushing and adds a version with the next push

steps.action: commits on a new branch `fix-retry` in a clone of workspace `demo` and runs `git push -o parley.change -o parley.title="Fix retry loop" origin fix-retry`
sends the command, the two push options and the pack to the receive-pack route with the agent's PAT
validates the push options, receives the pack, applies the push rules and writes `refs/heads/fix-retry`
finds no open change for the branch, opens change `demo#1` with version 1 and the given title, emits `parley.git.push` and answers with the line `change demo#1 version 1 (opened)`
prints `remote: change demo#1 version 1 (opened)` and exits 0
commits again and runs `git push origin fix-retry` without options
writes the ref, records version 2 of change `demo#1` and answers with the line `change demo#1 version 2`
reads `GET /workspaces/demo/changes/1` and sees version 2 with the pushed head

real_components: parleyd started in-process with its real router
git smart HTTP receive-pack and the push rules
setup: a hub started on 127.0.0.1:0 with a temporary data directory
a user with a ready workspace `demo` in organization `acme` and a PAT carrying git:write, changes:read and changes:write
a clone of the workspace's git URL made with the git client
end_state: the first push printed `remote: change demo#1 version 1 (opened)` and the second `remote: change demo#1 version 2`
immediately after the second `git push` returns, `GET /workspaces/demo/changes/1` shows title `Fix retry loop`, state `open`, version 2 and `head_sha` equal to the local head of `fix-retry`
`refs/parley/changes/1/1` and `refs/parley/changes/1/2` are fetchable from the hub
the event log holds two `parley.git.push` events for `refs/heads/fix-retry`
smoke.pseudocode: in test/e2e/push_change_test.go: hub = startHub(t); clone = gitClone(hub.gitURL('acme','demo'), pat); commit(clone, 'fix-retry'); out1 = git(clone, 'push', '-o', 'parley.change', '-o', 'parley.title=Fix retry loop', 'origin', 'fix-retry'); assert out1.exit == 0 and contains(out1.stderr, 'remote: change demo#1 version 1 (opened)'); commit(clone, 'fix-retry'); out2 = git(clone, 'push', 'origin', 'fix-retry'); assert contains(out2.stderr, 'remote: change demo#1 version 2'); ch = apiGet('/workspaces/demo/changes/1'); assert ch.version == 2 and ch.head_sha == revParse(clone, 'fix-retry') and ch.title == 'Fix retry loop'; assert git(clone, 'fetch', 'origin', 'refs/parley/changes/1/1', 'refs/parley/changes/1/2').exit == 0

execution_paths.title: A push to a task fork opens a change in the parent without any option

steps.action: clones a task fork of `demo` that has `auto_change` on, commits on a new branch `work` and runs `git push origin work`
sends the command and the pack to the fork's receive-pack route with the fork-bound PAT, with no push option
accepts the push, writes the branch in the fork and, because the fork has `auto_change` on, opens a change in `demo` with source `{fork slug, work}` and the fork's base branch as target
reads the change through `GET /workspaces/demo/changes/1` with the same token

real_components: parleyd started in-process with its real router
task fork creation with a minted token
git smart HTTP receive-pack and the push rules
setup: a hub started on 127.0.0.1:0 with a ready workspace `demo` whose default branch is `main`
a task fork of `demo` created over the API with `auto_change` true, `purpose` `speed up retries` and a token carrying git:write, changes:read and changes:write
end_state: `git push origin work` exited 0 and printed `remote: change demo#1 version 1 (opened)`
`GET /workspaces/demo/changes/1` shows `workspace_slug` `demo`, source `{workspace_slug: <fork slug>, branch: work}`, `target_branch` `main` and state `open`
the branch `work` exists in the fork and not in `demo`

execution_paths.title: A push with an invalid option is refused before anything is written

steps.action: runs `git push -o parley.titel=x origin topic` in a clone of workspace `demo`
sends the command, the push option and the pack to the receive-pack route with the developer's API key

validates the push options before receiving the pack, finds `parley.titel` unknown, stores nothing and answers with `ng refs/heads/topic invalid push option parley.titel: unknown option` and the side-band line `error: invalid push option parley.titel: unknown option`
prints `remote: error: invalid push option parley.titel: unknown option` and `! [remote rejected] topic -> topic (invalid push option parley.titel: unknown option)` and exits non-zero
